extracted.intended_audience: prospective authors, editors, and readers of Kvant/Quantum (mathematicians, teachers, advanced high-school students)
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and expectations for preparing feature articles, problems, and illustrations for the Russian popular-mathematics magazine Kvant (intended for high-school–level readership but sometimes containing advanced or original results).

rubrics_metrics.name: Conceptual, nontechnical exposition
rubrics_metrics.description: The feature articles were always conceptual, nontechnical and provided a substantial introduction to the subject.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should write in a manner similar to a good colloquium talk: emphasize intuition and concepts, de-emphasize heavy technicalities, and provide a substantial introduction that is accessible on first or repeated readings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assumed background level
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors may assume only familiarity with the standard high school mathematics and physics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do routine references to other 'Kvant' articles when needed, but keep the required prerequisites at high-school level so the broad readership (especially high-school students and teachers) can follow.

rubrics_metrics.name: High standards of exposition and heavy editorial revision
rubrics_metrics.description: Kvant had very high standards of exposition; the acceptance of an article by the Editorial Board was, in many cases, only the beginning of a serious work on it, including heavy editing, often complete revision and rewriting, sometimes jointly with the editors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be prepared for substantial editorial changes; the final published article may be dramatically different from the original submission. Authors should expect detailed editorial collaboration aimed at improving clarity and exposition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refereed submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Unlike many popular magazines, all submitted articles had been refereed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions undergo formal refereeing; editorial acceptance and refereeing are part of the quality-control process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasis on instructive examples and figures
rubrics_metrics.description: An instructive example is worth an abstract general theory; a figure is worth a thousand words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer concrete, illustrative examples and high-quality figures to long abstract development. Figures and visual exposition are highly valued and often critical to communicating ideas to Kvant's audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Connection of classical results with contemporary mathematics
rubrics_metrics.description: Classical results were connected, when possible, with contemporary mathematics (for example, Euler's theory of developable surfaces with modern singularity theory).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When treating classical material, indicate links to modern developments to broaden readers' perspective and show relevance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suitable topic types
rubrics_metrics.description: Feature articles ranged over classical mathematical gems, 20th-century mathematics, original mathematical results, biographical and historical pieces, and mathematical themes in art and poetry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Kvant published a wide variety of topics — from projective geometry theorems to quasicrystals and knot polynomials — so authors with both expository and original material may be appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plentiful, high-quality illustrations and art
rubrics_metrics.description: All illustrations—and they were plentiful—were in color; pictures accompanied articles and often related art with the mathematical and physical content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should provide clear material for illustrators (some artists requested a detailed explanation of the article). High-quality, sometimes radical artwork that ties to the content was encouraged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Problem Corner composition
rubrics_metrics.description: Every issue had a Problem Corner: five mathematical and five physical problems; their solutions would be published a few months later.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Problems should be suitable for the magazine's audience and timed with solution publication; since the 1980s the Problem Corner also included computer-science problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Volume and variety of problems
rubrics_metrics.description: Each issue contained 50–100 mathematical problems of various levels of difficulty, with or without solutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Problems should span a range of difficulties to engage both school-level readers and advanced problem-solvers; many problems served as preparation material for university entrance exams.

rubrics_metrics.name: Target readership profile
rubrics_metrics.description: Most readers were high school students and teachers; a significant portion were interested in preparation materials for university entrance examinations; other readers included undergraduates, graduate students, researchers, and the general public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write chiefly to engage high-school students and teachers while still providing material that can interest undergraduates and the broader mathematical public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Issue structure and section types
rubrics_metrics.description: A typical Kvant issue contained four feature articles (two in physics and two in mathematics), one or two shorter articles (e.g., 'Physics Lab' or 'Mathematical Circle'), a Problem Corner, and smaller sections (mathematical games, chess page, letters, book reviews); there was also 'Kvant for elementary schoolers'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When preparing submissions, consider which section is appropriate (feature article vs. short piece vs. Problem Corner vs. Kvant for younger readers).

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial resources and author compensation
rubrics_metrics.description: The magazine was published by large academies and staffed by about a dozen full-time editors (some with Ph.D.); authors were paid a relatively generous honorarium.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect a professional editorial process backed by institutional resources; high editorial standards matched with formal compensation for authors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encouragement of early independent research
rubrics_metrics.description: One did not have to wait until graduate school to start mathematical research; in fact, one could start even in high school.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions that enable or showcase independent research by younger readers (including original results accessible to school-age researchers) were in line with Kvant's mission.
